cases.prompt: We rolled back two different approaches to the payment retry queue design before a third approach finally worked and shipped. We're at a stable closeout point now -- extract the reusable learning from why the first two failed and decide where it should live.
expected_decisions: Attempt sequence reconstructed for materially different attempts only
expected_evidence: Contrast between the earlier attempts and the one that shipped
cases.notes: Two rolled-back approaches plus a third that shipped is materially-different-attempts closeout learning capture, not just a normal merge.

cases.prompt: A delegated worker's first attempt was rejected because it edited files outside its allowed scope; we rewrote the task brief with a tighter allowed-file list and a boundary note, and the second attempt was accepted. Now that the branch is stable, capture what should change so this scope miss doesn't happen again.
expected_decisions: Materially different attempt recognized (delegation boundary/allowed scope changed)
Learning scope classified project-specific or cross-project-reusable
Retention action chosen from the priority order, not a docs-only close if preventable and deterministic
expected_evidence: Rejected run record or judge result
cases.notes: A rejected-then-accepted delegated run with a changed delegation boundary is a materially different attempt, not routine review.

cases.prompt: Quality-gate rejected our completion claim because the only evidence was a manual eyeball check with no reproducible oracle; we changed the verification approach and re-routed the work through a different validation method before it passed. Now that it is closed out, capture the learning.
expected_decisions: Verification-method change recognized as a materially different attempt
Project-specific vs cross-project-reusable scope decided for the weak-oracle pattern
Retention action prefers lint/harness over prose for a deterministic gap
expected_evidence: Evidence of the changed verification method/oracle
cases.notes: A quality-gate rejection followed by a route/verification-method change is process learning this skill owns, not a second quality-gate run.

cases.prompt: This branch just hit the same failure signature we already wrote up in a retrospective a few weeks ago -- same failure class, same failed invariant, same earliest signal, same affected workflow boundary. Handle the retrospective side of closing this out.
expected_decisions: Recurrence marked repeated, not treated as a one-off
Repeated plus preventable rules out a docs-only close
expected_evidence: Reference to the prior retrospective record
Matching failure class, invariant, signal, and boundary
cases.notes: A recurring failure signature against a prior retrospective record is this skill's recurrence-search step and its repeated+preventable closure rule.

cases.prompt: 振り返りをして、Project固有と汎用の学びを分け、SKILL/Lint/Wikiへの反映先を決めて。
expected_decisions: Learning scope split into task-only, project-specific, and cross-project-reusable
cases.notes: Explicit request naming retrospective plus project-specific vs general-learning routing to Skill/Lint/Wiki; the one case allowed to name adjacent mechanisms explicitly.

cases.prompt: Fix the typo in the log message on line 42 of parser.py from 'recieved' to 'received' and commit.
cases.notes: A one-line typo fix is clean first-pass work; no rollback, no attempts, no rejection.

cases.prompt: The deploy script failed with a connection timeout to the registry; I reran the exact same deploy command and it succeeded this time.
cases.notes: A transient network retry of the identical command is explicitly not a materially different attempt.

cases.prompt: The login endpoint throws a 500 on empty passwords. Reproduce it, find the root cause, fix it, and verify.
cases.notes: Single-incident RCA stays inside bug-investigation-and-rca; no rollback, no multiple attempts, no misrouting.

cases.prompt: The registered experiment testing whether caching the embeddings improves latency came back disconfirmed as expected -- no speedup. Log the result and move to the next probe.
cases.notes: One expected disconfirmed result is ordinary negative evidence handled per-experiment, not a retrospective trigger.

cases.prompt: All checks pass and review is approved. Merge the PR and delete the local and remote feature branch.
cases.notes: A clean merge and cleanup with no rollback or repeated failed attempt is branch-completion's ordinary lifecycle, not a retrospective trigger.

cases.prompt: Address the reviewer's comments on this PR: rename the two variables they flagged and split the long function as requested, then reply to each thread.
cases.notes: Ordinary review-comment accept/refute processing is not a retrospective trigger even though it changes code after feedback.
